ruling.recommended_action: Hold the automatic distance refund; route the case to a Ryde human reviewer for the SAFE-1 abuse finding on F9 (driver telling the rider to shut up), and include the route-deviation fare computation (5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25 voucher) in the file so the human can execute the refund of $7.25 once the account/conduct review is concluded.
ruling.reasoning:
Route: the trip is RydeTAXI, metered, so detour kilometres flow into the fare, and the trace settles that exactly one off-route segment exists, F3 (09:00–09:11, 6.89 km driven against 1.75 km optimal, +5.14 km, up to 1481 m off the optimal route) [F3][RD-1]. No exemption is available: the trace fails RD-4(a) (no incident recorded near the route, F14; the only traffic records are PIE band 5 and KPE band 4, F12, F13, neither band 1 nor 2, which under RD-4(b) cannot exempt on its own, and the driver expressly does not press congestion) [F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. The driver's post-trip "the GPS rerouted" is a statement, not traffic evidence or consent (G11) [F11][RD-4][RD-5].

Consent: RD-3 is inapplicable — no rider-requested stop is measured in the segment, so RD-3(a)/(b) give the driver nothing [F3][RD-3]. On RD-5, the chat is complete and fully timestamped (F10) and the only rider message is at 09:04, after the segment began at 09:00, asking why the route differed (F8); the driver's 09:05 reply is not consent (F9); and no driver-proposed route agreement exists in the record [F8][F9][F10][F11][RD-5]. Scope therefore reads as "no agreement before the segment" — counts, and the segment is un-exempt [F3][RD-5].

Amount, per the trace's formula: non-exempt extra_km × this trip's rate (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km) = 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.2484 → $7.25; the rate is the fare record's own figure (F4 prices 5.55 km at $1.4102/km) and only F3's attributed 5.14 km is claimed [F3][F4][RD-2]. The dissimilarity with the fare-side 5.55 km is corridor mileage not attributed to any segment and is not refundable [F4][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting line is a metered waiting unit in a completed RydeTAXI run and is chargeable, not refunded [F5][F7][RD-3(c)]. No unpublished add-on is billed, so FARE-1 yields nothing further [F6][F7][FARE-1].

However, the safety screen is not clean. Reading F9 in context — "Shut up and let me drive.", sent one minute after the rider's reasonable route question (F8) — this is hostile, abusive language aimed at the other party, which Ryde's code of conduct bars as "abuse of any kind" [F8][F9][SAFE-1]. I do not accept a reading that it is abuse of the rider in the SAFE-1 sense without noting it is at least "suspected", including the rider's stated feeling of being unsafe during an unexplained 11-minute, 5.14 km deviation (F3, complaint) [F3][SAFE-1]. The screen is asymmetric: because it is at least suspected, no automatic ruling is issued and the whole matter goes to a human reviewer, whose summary is: RydeTAXI MBS→Tampines Mall, 08:48–09:21; single off-route segment 09:00–09:11 with +5.14 km (F3); no RD-4 exemption (F12–F14); no rider consent before the segment (F8–F11); driver's abusive reply at 09:05 (F9); the fare finding of $7.25 should be executed as a voucher once the conduct review concludes (NS-7) [RD-2][NS-7][SAFE-1].

Evidence: sufficient — the trace's measure of the segment, the fare record and a complete timestamped chat settle every element the fare and consent findings need [F3][F4][F7][F10]. Confidence reflects that the clauses apply clearly to these facts; the case is nonetheless escalated because SAFE-1 screens it out of automatic disposition [SAFE-1].

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 09:00–09:11, 6.89 km driven against 1.75 km optimal (+5.14 km). It is un-exempt: RD-4(a) fails (no incident near the route, F14; PIE band 5 and KPE band 4 are not band 1/2, so RD-4(b) cannot exempt alone) and no rider consent precedes the segment — the complete, timestamped chat (F10) contains only the 09:04 question (F8) and the 09:05 driver reply (F9), and the driver's post-trip reroute claim (F11) is a statement, not consent (G11). RD-3 is inapplicable as no rider-named stop is measured here. Counts under RD-2: 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25.

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected on its merits but superseded: I read F9 ('Shut up and let me drive.') in the context of the rider's 09:04 question (F8) as abusive language aimed at the rider, which SAFE-1 treats as at least 'suspected' and routes to a person rather than to an automatic refund — so the relief granted is escalation, not the auto-executed refund requested.

Not rejected as a reading, but the safety element cannot be disposed of here: F9 read with F8 is an SAFE-1 matter, so the case is escalated instead of deciding the fare alone; the $7.25 computation is preserved for the human reviewer via RD-2.

The driver's own fallback is not accepted: I do read F9, against the rider's 09:04 question (F8), as abuse under SAFE-1 ('abuse of any kind'), which is at least 'suspected'; the disposition is therefore escalation, not a standalone fare ruling as the driver urged.

Correct as far as it goes — F17 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6's 'repeated' gateway for flag_account is not met and no account flag attaches on this record — but this does not affect the escalation, which rests on SAFE-1 (F8, F9).
Agreed and moot: F16/F17 show no upheld route dispute in 90 days, so RD-6 yields no flag_account; the escalation here is conduct-based under SAFE-1, not a repeated-breach account action.

Accepted: F1/F2/F3 establish the deviation and I record it under RD-1; the segment finding is 'counts' as the claimant argues, but the ruling cannot be executed automatically because the same record triggers SAFE-1.

Accepted on consent (no rider message before 09:00, F8/F10; F11 is not consent under G11), which supports the 'counts' finding for F3 under RD-5, but the claim's request for a self-executing refund is declined in favour of escalation.
Accepted as to quantum: 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25 under the RD-2 metered branch; withheld from automatic execution only because of the SAFE-1 screen.
